context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “Condemned, delivered, mocked, and killed” preserves a distinct parallel witness source unit within anticipation.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: As the group goes up to Jerusalem, Jesus again takes the Twelve and states a sequence of condemnation, delivery, mockery, abuse, death, and rising.
observations.label: Condemned, delivered, mocked, and killed: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps jesus, twelve, gentiles visible within its Crucifixion evidence.
observations.label: Condemned, delivered, mocked, and killed: action, promise, or consequence

payload.posture: Read Mark 10:32–34 as its own anticipation and stated approach crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: This witness selects its own people, actions, words, and sequence around the Crucifixion without explaining every difference from the other witnesses.
payload.title: Condemned, delivered, mocked, and killed
